name: Whalesync
description:
Whalesync keeps data in sync between the tools your team already uses —
Airtable, Webflow, HubSpot, Salesforce, Notion, Postgres, and more — with
two-way sync that feels native in every app.

With this connector, Claude can set up and run syncs for you: create a sync
between two apps, map tables and fields, validate the mapping, and turn the
sync on. Once data is flowing, Claude can monitor it — check sync status,
find out why a record isn’t syncing, review held deletes, and retry failed
work after you fix the cause.

Connecting your apps and approving anything irreversible always stays in
your hands: OAuth connections, starting a sync, and approving deletes happen
in the Whalesync app, and Claude hands you a link at each of those steps.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Whalesync creates live two-way syncs between apps (Airtable, Webflow, HubSpot, Postgres, Notion, …). You build and monitor syncs; the data then flows on its own.

The flow that works:
1. sync_list_connectors — find the two connectors and what auth each needs.
2. sync_create — NEVER ask a person for credentials in chat. The default for every connector is connector name ONLY (no auth, no base): the sync comes back with a browser link per unconnected side where the person enters credentials or signs in securely in the app. OAuth connectors allow nothing else (the person picks the base in the browser, and even a remote_id known from another sync cannot be pre-selected); for API-key connectors include auth inline only when the credentials were already handed to you programmatically.
3. If the sync reports pending_actions: relay each url and instruction to the person VERBATIM, then poll sync_get until the side is connected. Never fetch those urls yourself — they are browser steps only a person can do.
4. sync_list_tables / sync_list_fields — read both sides' schemas (these can block up to a minute while a fetch runs).
5. sync_validate_mappings, then sync_update_mappings. Reference tables and fields by remote id, not name. Use {"create": {"name": "…"}} to have Whalesync create a missing table or field on the other side.
6. A sync only runs under mappings a person has reviewed and started: relay the user_confirmation pending action (review_url), then poll sync_get until status is active.
7. Monitor with sync_get_status, sync_list_operations, and sync_list_issues; sync_retry_issue after fixing an issue's remediation — an issue is what blocks syncing, so that tool is also how you "retry syncing" a record someone asks about. When a person asks about one specific record ("why isn't my Airtable record syncing?"), use sync_search_records then sync_get_record_status.
8. Deletes wait for a person. A record that goes missing on one side does not get deleted on the other until someon

tool.name: sync_list_pending_deletes
tool.title: List pending deletes
tool.description: Deletes waiting on a person for one sync. When a record goes missing on one side, Whalesync holds the delete rather than applying it to the other side, so an accidental delete or an app outage cannot destroy data. Each entry links to the record in the connected app so a person can look before deciding. Approving or ignoring is irreversible and deliberately not in this API — relay the entry's review_url. A sync that auto-approves deletes has no queue and answers delete_approval_disabled; sync_get reports which mode a sync is in before you call.

state.description: Defaults to awaiting_review. "ignored" lists the deletes a person chose to keep the record for — dormant, but not resolved.

tool.name: sync_retry_issue
tool.title: Retry an issue
tool.description: Re-attempts the failed work behind an issue. An issue is what holds a record or table back, so clearing it is how syncing runs again — "retry syncing", "sync that record again" and "try it again" all mean this tool, and there is no other retry. Fix the cause (see remediation) first, or it fails the same way. When a person names a record instead of an issue, sync_search_records then sync_get_record_status name the issue blocking it; sync_list_issues lists them for a whole sync.

tool.name: sync_get_record_status
tool.title: Get a record's sync status
tool.description: Everything known about one record's sync state — the diagnosis tool for "why isn't this record syncing". Returns open issues blocking it, a pending delete awaiting a person's review, operations queued right now, per-side flags (deleted / filtered out by a sync filter / sync disabled), links to the record in both apps, and its most recent operations. queued_operations null means the queue could not be consulted, not that it is empty. For older history call sync_list_operations with record. Diagnose from the flags and issues before assuming the sync itself is broken: a filtered or sync-disabled record is excluded on purpose, and a pending delete waits for a person to approve it in the app.

tool.name: sync_create
tool.title: Create a sync
tool.description: Creates a draft sync between two connectors. NEVER ask the person for credentials in chat: create the sync with connector names only (no auth, no base) and it comes back with a pending_actions link per side where the person connects securely in the app — relay each link. That is the only option for OAuth connectors (the person picks the base in the browser; even a remote_id you know from another sync cannot be pre-selected), and the default for API-key connectors too; include auth inline only when the credentials were already handed to you programmatically. Validation reports the first problem it finds, so fix and retry rather than expecting every issue at once. Not idempotent: if a call fails ambiguously, check sync_list before retrying.

tool.name: sync_update_mappings
tool.title: Replace the mappings
tool.description: Replaces the whole mappings document (fetch with sync_get_mappings, modify, send back — there is no partial edit). Validate first with sync_validate_mappings. Referenced tables whose fields were never fetched are fetched during the call, so a first update can take a few seconds. The sync must be paused or draft.

tables.description: The full mappings document's tables array. Each tables[] entry: {left_table, right_table, direction: "left_to_right"|"right_to_left"|"two_way", left?: {view?, record_delete_behavior?}, right?: {…}, fields: [{left_field, right_field, direction?}]}. Table/field references are remote ids (preferred), prefixed ids, or exact names — or {"create": {"name": "…"}} to have Whalesync create the table/field on the other side (a created table requires all its fields to be creates too; only one side of any pair may be a create). view is REQUIRED for sides whose table reports views in sync_list_tables (Airtable, Salesforce): pass a value from views.options, or "ALL_RECORDS" for the whole table — omitting view CLEARS a prior selection. record_delete_behavior is "sync" (default) or "do_nothing", and says what a delete on the OTHER side does to records in this table — "do_nothing" is Delete Protection for this table. A pair may also report filter and advanced_settings: these are READ-ONLY (set in the app, ignored on write) but explain why records are skipped — each carries a plain-English summary/description and a docs link.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Whalesync to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Whalesync to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.whalesync.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Whalesync MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Whalesync scores 96/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Whalesync's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Whalesync scores 80/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 46 of 46 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Whalesync MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whalesync lists 24 MCP tools, including activate_sync, create_sync, delete_sync, get_issue, get_mappings, get_operation, get_record_status, get_sync, get_sync_status, list_bases, list_connectors, and list_fields.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Whalesync?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Whalesync in automation-workflows on the Manufact MCP catalog include Sidewave Maggiordomo, Corsair Cloud, Fleet Workspace, typenode-mcp, and tinyfish.
Whalesync requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

_published_faq.name: How can Whalesync improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: live_export_validate_mappings is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 61/100. No output schema is declared.
